item.title: Interpreting Performance Test Results
item.description:
When a performance test finishes, Meshery analyzes the results and stores them under the test’s profile in the Cloud Native Performance (SMP) format. You can view, download, and compare them.

Read a result

Open Performance → Profiles, open a profile, and select a result. The chart shows the latency distribution as a histogram, with the percentiles (such as p50, p90, and p99) and the achieved queries per second.

Latency and throughput are the two signals to examine first. A rising p99 with a steady p50 usually points to contention or queuing that affects only some requests.

item.title: Managing Performance
item.description:
Measuring and managing performance is key to operating any infrastructure efficiently. Meshery organizes that work around performance profiles. For step-by-step instructions on running a test, see Performance Management with Meshery.

Performance Profiles

A performance profile saves a load test’s configuration so you can run the same test again and track how performance changes over time. With profiles you can:

  1. Save a test configuration and rerun it from Meshery UI or with mesheryctl perf apply <profile-name>.
  2. Keep every result of a test in one place, under its profile.
  3. Rename a profile that started as an ad hoc test so you can reuse it.

Load Generators

Meshery runs tests with fortio, a fast, small, embeddable Go load testing library and command-line tool. Meshery’s load generator interface is extensible to support others.

item.title: Performance Management with Meshery
item.description:
Use this guide to measure the latency and throughput of a service with Meshery. You run a load test against an HTTP or HTTPS endpoint, save its settings as a performance profile so you can repeat it, and compare the results across runs. Run tests from Meshery UI, from mesheryctl, or from your CI pipeline.

Before you begin

  • A running Meshery Server that you are signed in to. See Installation.
  • An endpoint that Meshery Server can reach, such as a service in a cluster that Meshery manages.
  • For mesheryctl, a signed-in context. See Authenticate with Meshery via CLI.

Run a test from Meshery UI

  1. Open Performance → Profiles.

item.title: Using Metrics in Meshery
item.description:
View metrics in Meshery

Meshery integrates with Grafana and Prometheus so you can visualize the health and resource usage of your cloud native infrastructure without leaving Meshery.

Metrics visualization lives in the dedicated Telemetry section of Meshery. Rather than entering a Grafana or Prometheus URL and API key into a settings form, you register Grafana and Prometheus as Meshery Connections (each with an associated Credential), and Telemetry queries them on your behalf - proxying every request securely through the Meshery server.
